newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt ends little changed, eyes on US payrolls.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt ends little changed, eyes on US payrolls.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices rose early but ended roughly unchanged as investors returning from IMF/World Bank meetings operated cautiously ahead of Friday's U.S. payrolls report, traders said.
"Clients have been getting more active again," said the chief Brady Trader at a U.S. money center bank. "They are not more active because we had an important figure tomorrow."
A market friendly U.S. payrolls figure for September, which is forecast to rise 166,000 jobs, could cause the Brady bond market to rise again.
"If tomorrow's figure is not awful we'll see prices rally," one trader said. "I think there is cash waiting for this. Everyone is going into the numebr with flat positions."
A Brady bond trader at a European bank said the market has had its fill of headlines from official sources in Washington and could hardly wait for the U.S. jobs data.
"Activity with clients was almost zero," the trader said. "Some people are just squaring positions. The number is more important for the traders."
Argentine FRBs edged up 1/4 to 84-1/2 bid, while Brazilian Cs were unchanged at 71-1/4.

"Everyone is waiting for payrolls but maybe when that comes we'll be waiting for something else," said Ingrid Iversen, debt strategist at UBS Securities. "Trade is not very inspiring. its not driven by fundmanetals
One Brady trader said that Peru's debt seemed well offered as investors seemed incliuned to buy Panama's paper for Peruvian.
